title: Reserve stock when orders are placed and cancelled
request: Make stock follow orders. (1) Add GET /products, answering { "items": [...] } with every product as { "sku", "name", "unitCents", "stock" }, in catalog order. (2) POST /orders now takes each line's quantity out of its product's stock. Before anything changes, check the cart's lines in cart order: a SKU that isn't in the catalog answers 422 with { "error": "Unknown SKU <SKU>" }, and a quantity above the product's stock answers 409 with { "error": "Not enough stock for <SKU>" }. The first line that fails decides the answer, and a refused order changes nothing: no order is created, the cart keeps its lines and no stock moves. (3) Add POST /orders/:id/cancel: a pending or paid order becomes "cancelled", its quantities go back to stock, and the answer is 200 with the order. Cancelling a shipped or an already cancelled order answers 409 with { "error": "A <status> order cannot be cancelled" } (e.g. "A shipped order cannot be cancelled"), and an unknown order answers 404 with { "error": "Order not found" }. (4) A cancelled order can't be paid or shipped: 409 with { "error": "A cancelled order cannot be paid" } or { "error": "A cancelled order cannot be shipped" }. (5) GET /reports/daily-total leaves cancelled orders out.

title: Apply multi-buy promotions and show them on the receipt
request: POST /orders applies two automatic promotions. "Apples 3 for 2": every third unit of APL-GALA-1KG in the order is free (7 units: 2 free). "Coffee and milk": each pair of one COF-BEAN-500 and one MLK-OAT-1L takes $1.50 off (3 bags of coffee and 2 oat milks: 2 pairs, $3.00 off). Every order now has "discountCents" (the sum of the promotions, 0 when none applies) and "promotions": a list of { "name", "discountCents" } with one entry per promotion that applied, in the order above (not in the order of the lines), using the names "Apples 3 for 2" and "Coffee and milk". subtotalCents stays the sum of the lines before any discount. For every order, with or without promotions, taxCents is 8% of (subtotalCents - discountCents), rounded half up to the cent once for the whole order, not line by line; totalCents = subtotalCents - discountCents + taxCents. The receipt prints one line per applied promotion right after the Subtotal line and before the Tax line, as "<name> -$4.50" (the name, two spaces, then the discount as a negative dollar amount); a receipt without promotions keeps its lines. The daily total adds up the new totalCents.

title: Report sales by the store's local day, with daylight saving time
request: Fernhill Market is in New York, so its reports must follow the store's calendar day in the America/New_York time zone, daylight saving time included. Orders keep createdAt in UTC. (1) GET /reports/daily-total?date=YYYY-MM-DD adds up the totalCents of the orders placed during that local day: an order at 2026-11-20T03:30:00Z belongs to 2026-11-19. It now also refuses dates that don't exist, like 2026-02-30, with the 400 it already gives for a bad format ({ "error": "date must be YYYY-MM-DD" }). (2) Add GET /reports/sales?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD, answering { "from", "to", "days": [{ "date", "orders", "totalCents" }], "totalCents" }: one entry per local day from `from` to `to`, both included, in date order, where orders is the number of orders placed that day and totalCents the sum of their totalCents; a day without orders still appears, with 0 and 0. The top-level totalCents is the sum over the days. from and to must both be real dates in YYYY-MM-DD, from must not be after to, and the range can't cover more than 31 days; otherwise answer 400 with { "error": "from and to must be real dates (YYYY-MM-DD), from <= to, at most 31 days" }.

title: Ship a paid order in several shipments
request: Let a paid order ship in parts. Add POST /orders/:id/shipments with { "lines": [{ "sku": "<SKU>", "quantity": <n> }] }. Every order now has "shipped", an object with the units shipped so far for each SKU of the order (0 for every SKU when the order is placed), and "shipments", the list of shipments in the order they were made (empty when placed), each { "id", "lines", "at" }: id is "shp_1", "shp_2" and so on, numbered within the order; lines is the shipped lines as { "sku", "quantity" }; at is the app clock's time as an ISO string. The order's own lines don't change. Checks, in this order: an unknown order answers 404 with { "error": "Order not found" }; only a paid or partially shipped order takes a shipment, any other answers 409 with { "error": "A <status> order cannot be shipped" } (e.g. "A pending order cannot be shipped"); lines must be a non-empty array of { sku, quantity } with distinct SKUs and whole quantities of 1 or more, else 400 with { "error": "lines must be a non-empty list of { sku, quantity }" }; a SKU that isn't in the order, or a quantity above what is left to ship of it, answers 422 with { "error": "Cannot ship <quantity> of <SKU>" } for the first such line. A refused shipment records nothing. An accepted one answers 201 with the order, whose status is "partially_shipped" while units are left and "shipped" once every unit has shipped. POST /orders/:id/ship keeps working for paid and partially shipped orders (200 with the order, 409 as above otherwise): it records one shipment of everything left, with the lines that still have units in the order's line order, and the order becomes "shipped". A partially shipped order can't be paid: 409 with { "error": "A partially_shipped order cannot be paid" }. The receipt doesn't change.

title: Earn and redeem loyalty points on orders
request: Add loyalty points. Every customer starts with 0 points. Add GET /customers/:id, answering { "id", "name", "email", "points" }, or 404 with { "error": "Customer not found" } for an unknown id. When an order is paid (POST /orders/:id/pay), its customer earns 1 point per whole dollar of (subtotalCents - discountCents), rounded down: $14.99 earns 14 points. Points are earned at payment only, never when the order is placed. POST /orders accepts an optional "redeemPoints". 100 points are worth $1.00, so one point is one cent. redeemPoints must be a whole number of 0 or more, a multiple of 100, no more than the customer's points and no more than the order's subtotalCents; otherwise answer 422 with { "error": "Cannot redeem <redeemPoints> points" } (the value as sent, e.g. "Cannot redeem 150 points") and change nothing: no order is created, the cart keeps its lines and no points move. The redeemed points leave the customer's balance when the order is placed. Every order now has "pointsRedeemed" (0 when none) and "discountCents" (equal to pointsRedeemed). For every order, with or without points, taxCents is 8% of (subtotalCents - discountCents), rounded half up to the cent once for the whole order, not line by line, and totalCents = subtotalCents - discountCents + taxCents. When points were redeemed, the receipt prints "Points -$1.00" (the discount as a negative dollar amount, after two spaces) right after the Subtotal line and before the Tax line; otherwise the receipt keeps its lines.

title: Make placing and paying for orders safe to retry
request: Make POST /orders and POST /orders/:id/pay safe to retry with an Idempotency-Key header. Without the header nothing changes. The key must be 1 to 64 characters, each a letter, a digit, "-" or "_"; any other value (an empty one included) answers 400 with { "error": "Invalid Idempotency-Key" } and does nothing. Keys are remembered per path: the same key can be used once on POST /orders and once on POST /orders/ord_0001/pay. The first request with a key runs as usual; if its answer is a success (2xx), the app remembers the request's JSON body and the answer (status and body). A later request with the same key, on the same path and with an equal JSON body (same values, whatever the order of the object's keys) gets the remembered status and body again, with the header "Idempotent-Replayed: true", and nothing runs again: no second order, no second payment. Answers that aren't replays don't have that header. The same key with a different body answers 422 with { "error": "Idempotency-Key reused with a different request" }. An answer that isn't a success isn't remembered, so the client can fix the problem and retry with the same key. A remembered key lasts 24 hours from its first request, on the app's clock (createApp({ now })): from exactly 24 hours on, it works like a new key.

title: Accept returns of shipped orders with fair refunds
request: Customers can return items from a shipped order within 30 days. Add POST /orders/:id/returns with { "lines": [{ "sku": "<SKU>", "quantity": <n> }] }. Checks, in this order: an unknown order answers 404 with { "error": "Order not found" }; an order that isn't shipped answers 409 with { "error": "A <status> order cannot be returned" } (e.g. "A paid order cannot be returned"); the app clock must be less than 30 days (30 x 24 hours) after the order's createdAt, else 409 with { "error": "The return window has closed" }; lines must be a non-empty array of { sku, quantity } with distinct SKUs and whole quantities of 1 or more, else 400 with { "error": "lines must be a non-empty list of { sku, quantity }" }; a SKU that isn't in the order, or more units than are left to return of it (bought minus already returned), answers 422 with { "error": "Cannot return <quantity> of <SKU>" } for the first such line. A refused return records nothing. An accepted return answers 201 with the order and puts the returned units back into each product's stock in the store (db.products). The refund of a return is the value of its lines (unitCents x quantity) plus their share of the order's tax: taxCents x (value of the returned lines) / subtotalCents, rounded half up to the cent. But the return that brings back the last units of the order refunds exactly what is left of totalCents, so the refunds of an order always add up to its totalCents. Every order has "returns", the list of its returns in order (empty until the first one), each { "id", "lines", "refundCents", "at" } with id "ret_1", "ret_2" and so on within the order, lines as sent, and at the app clock's time as an ISO string; and "refundedCents", the sum of its refunds (0 until the first return). Once every unit has been returned, the order's status becomes "returned".

title: Change product prices without touching placed orders
request: Prices can change. Add POST /products/:sku/price with { "unitCents": <n> }: n must be a whole number above 0, else 400 with { "error": "unitCents must be a whole number above 0" }; an unknown SKU answers 404 with { "error": "Product not found" }; the answer is 200 with the product { "sku", "name", "unitCents", "stock" }. Add GET /products/:sku/prices, answering { "sku", "history": [{ "unitCents", "from" }] } (404 as above for an unknown SKU): the first entry is the catalog price with "from": null, then one entry per change, oldest first, with from set to the app clock's time as an ISO string. Setting the price a product already has records nothing (and still answers 200 with the product). Carts always show today's prices: GET /carts/:id and the answer to POST /carts/:id/items show every line at the product's current unitCents, with lineCents = unitCents x quantity; cart lines keep their shape { sku, name, unitCents, quantity, lineCents }. When an order is placed, its lines take the prices of that moment, so a change made after an item went into the cart still counts. Once placed, an order never changes: a later price change leaves the order, its receipt and the daily total as they were.

title: Filter, sort and page the order list
request: GET /orders takes optional query parameters that combine: status (pending, paid or shipped); customer (a customer id, exact match; any text is accepted); from and to (dates in YYYY-MM-DD: only orders whose createdAt falls on or after from, and on or before to, by its UTC date); minTotal (a whole number of cents, 0 or more: only orders with totalCents >= minTotal); sort (createdAt, -createdAt, total or -total; default createdAt; a leading "-" means newest or largest first, and orders that tie are always ordered by id ascending, whatever the direction); limit (a whole number from 1 to 100, default 20); offset (a whole number, 0 or more, default 0). Filters apply first, then the sort, then offset and limit. The answer is { "items": [...], "total": <how many orders match, before offset and limit>, "limit": <the limit used>, "offset": <the offset used> }. An invalid value answers 400 with { "error": "Invalid query: <name>" }, naming the first invalid parameter in the order of this list (status, from, to, minTotal, sort, limit, offset). A date that doesn't exist, like 2026-02-30, is invalid, and a to before from makes to invalid. A parameter that isn't in the list also answers 400 with { "error": "Invalid query: <name>" }, but only once every known parameter is valid.

title: Sell gift cards and accept them as payment
request: Add gift cards. POST /gift-cards with { "amountCents": <n> } creates one: n must be a whole number from 500 to 50000, else 400 with { "error": "amountCents must be a whole number from 500 to 50000" }. The answer is 201 with { "code", "balanceCents" }, where codes are "GC-0001", "GC-0002" and so on, in the order the cards are created. GET /gift-cards/:code answers the card, or 404 with { "error": "Gift card not found" }. Codes match ignoring case, here and on orders. POST /orders accepts an optional "giftCard" with a code. A gift card is a payment, not a discount: subtotalCents, taxCents and totalCents don't change. The order takes min(balance, totalCents) off the card's balance. Every order now has "giftCard" (the card's code in upper case, or null without a card), "giftCardCents" (the amount taken from the card, 0 without one) and "amountDueCents" (totalCents - giftCardCents). When amountDueCents is 0, the order is placed with the status "paid". An unknown code answers 404 with { "error": "Gift card not found" }, and a card with a balance of 0 answers 422 with { "error": "Gift card is empty" }; a refused order changes nothing: no order is created, the cart keeps its lines and no balance moves. When a card was used, the receipt prints two more lines right after the Total line, like "Gift card GC-0001 -$5.00" and "Amount due $11.19" (two spaces before each amount).
